Step-1:  Calculate the number of moles supplied by each reagent  
• CH₃COOH : 0.1 M × 0.500 L = 0.050 mol (weak acid)  
• HCl : 0.2 M × 0.400 L = 0.080 mol H⁺ (strong acid)  
• Ba(OH)₂ : 0.3 M × 0.300 L = 0.090 mol Ba(OH)₂ → 0.090 × 2 = 0.180 mol OH⁻ (strong base)

Step-2:  Neutralise strong acid with strong base first  
OH⁻ remaining after neutralising H⁺:  
0.180 mol − 0.080 mol = 0.100 mol OH⁻ left.

Step-3:  Neutralise the weak acid with the remaining OH⁻  
CH₃COOH + OH⁻ → CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O  
0.050 mol CH₃COOH consumes 0.050 mol OH⁻, producing 0.050 mol CH₃COO⁻.  
OH⁻ still left unreacted:  
0.100 mol − 0.050 mol = 0.050 mol.

(The extra OH⁻ dominates; the weak base CH₃COO⁻ contributes only ~5 × 10⁻⁶ M OH⁻, which is negligible compared to 0.041 M.)

Step-4:  Calculate [OH⁻] in the final 1.20 L mixture  
[OH⁻] = 0.050 mol / 1.20 L = 0.0417 M.

Step-5:  Find pOH and pH  
pOH = –log(0.0417) ≈ 1.38  
pH = 14 – 1.38 = 12.62

Therefore, the pH of the resulting solution is 12.62.

Answer: C
